MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH — TERMLY EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conservation of marine and freshwater environments? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.

5. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Reproduction.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Reproduction.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Reproduction.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Reproduction.

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conservation of Marine and Freshwater Environments 3.2 Weather and Climatic Cond? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conservation of Marine and Freshwater Environments 3.2 Weather and Climatic Cond.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conservation of Marine and Freshwater Environments 3.2 Weather and Climatic Cond.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Conservation of Marine and Freshwater Environments 3.2 Weather and Climatic Cond.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conservation of Marine and Freshwater Environments 3.2 Weather and Climatic Cond.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Record keeping in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Record keeping in aquaculture.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Record keeping in aquaculture.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Record keeping in aquaculture.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.

13. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Weather and Climatic Conditions in Marine and Freshwater 3.3 Fishery by-products.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish feeds and feeding? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish feeds and feeding.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish feeds and feeding.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Fish feeds and feeding.
